Title: Wild Hogs
Content: In `text(1530)`, Spanish explorer Hernando de Soto traveled through what is now `14` different states, including Mississippi. The explorer brought along pigs (hogs) as a food source. Throughout the `3text(,)100text(-mile)` journey, some of the hogs escaped into the wild. These hogs were previously not part of the Mississippi ecosystem and became known as wild hogs. They are classified as an invasive species and cause large amounts of damage to the ecosystem throughout the `text(Southeast)` to this day. They use their tusks and hoofs to search for food, which destroys plant life. Wild hogs are omnivores, which means they eat both producers and consumers. There is very little that wild hogs will not eat.
The model shows the position of wild hogs in a Mississippi food web.
Humans have made attempts to reduce the numbers of wild hogs. Some methods include using fencing to keep wild hogs out of livestock areas, trapping, and hunting with dogs.
